critical_facts.description: Share of promoted volume bought by customers who also buy at full price

required_conclusions.description: Promotions mostly subsidise purchases that would happen anyway (71%, post-promo dip) — volume shifted, not created (total +2.1%)
Snacks and household promotions destroy margin (negative incremental margin)
Cut / reshape promotions (less depth, fewer in snacks and household, keep where incremental margin is positive)

traps.description: Accepting that promotions drove growth and raising the budget 20%
Presenting promoted-volume growth (+14%) as total growth (+2.1%) (v2 terms: promoted-volume growth stated as such is correct)

reference_governing_thought: Promotions now drive 38% of sales but mostly subsidise customers who would buy anyway; cutting deep promotions in snacks and household and keeping them where they pay recovers margin at little volume cost.
notes: Total volume grew only 2.1% while promoted volume grew 14% and full-price volume fell 6%: a shift, not growth.
